posts.caption:
A girl’s silence is written into the law as a yes.

In May 2026 the Taliban issued Decree No. 18. It sets no minimum age for marriage, eligibility is tied to puberty, which can begin at nine. It treats a girl’s silence as her consent, and makes leaving a husband nearly impossible for a woman while leaving it simple for a man.

Women are banned from working as lawyers and judges. There is no one in that courtroom who has ever been a girl.
She cannot go to school past twelve. She cannot refuse. And saying nothing is recorded as agreement.
Five years. A hundred decrees. This is the newest one.

Cruelty has a paper trail. We publish it.

posts.title: A girl’s silence is written into the law as a yes.

posts.caption:
45 countries banned the test. Nobody banned the ingredient.

Cosmetic animal testing is prohibited across the EU and dozens of other markets. The chemicals inside those cosmetics can still be tested on animals under separate chemical-safety law, assessed for worker exposure and environmental risk, filed with a different regulator, counted in a different column.

Same substance. Same animal. A ban that stops at the product and not the molecule.
The label says cruelty-free. The ingredient dossier says otherwise.

Cruelty has a paper trail. We publish it.

Your clothes are wrinkle-free. The labour isn’t.

Who washes it?
Who irons it?
Who repairs it?
Who keeps everything running while everyone else gets to look “put together”?

Women have carried generations of unpaid domestic labour behind the scenes, work treated as instinct, obligation, or simply “what women do.”

Animals are treated no differently by the industries that use them, bred, tested, confined and exploited because their bodies are considered useful.

The fashion industry sells the finished image.

Someone still has to do the work.
Someone always carries the cost.

Invisible labour is still labour.
Invisible cruelty is still cruelty.

Dismantling the propaganda.

Your mascara has a half-life.

82% of waterproof mascaras test positive for forever chemicals. Almost none say so on the label.
The FDA reviewed them and admitted it cannot say whether they’re safe.

They’ve been found in 625 animal species on every continent. Polar bears. Dolphins. Tigers. None of them bought the product.

Read the label. Skip “waterproof.”

posts.caption:
LAWS OFF OUR BODIES - every body.

The sign was written for women. It was always about more than women.

For centuries, the law has decided what a body is allowed to do with itself, whether it can leave, whether it can refuse, whether it belongs to the state, the husband, the industry, or the farmer. Reproductive rights have been rolled back or restricted across dozens of countries in the last decade. And in every country on earth, the law still permits the branding, castration and slaughter of animals for profit.

Different bodies. Same legislation. Same architecture.

The megaphone is loud because the paper trail is not enough. Sometimes the record has to be read out in the street.

FERAL FEMME · Dismantling the Propaganda.

The fur is fake. The clothes are secondhand. The coat came from someone’s grandmother. Nothing in this photograph killed anything. Nothing in this photograph was bought new.

The industry loses money when women share. The animals live longer when women stop buying.

She is not posing with wildlife. She is posing with the survivors of a supply chain designed to look like affection.

They have been skinning women for centuries. They just call it a treatment now.

The peel. The laser. The retinol. The filler. The bleach. The tuck. Every one of them removes a layer of a woman and calls the removal an upgrade. What she was underneath, the years, the ink, the animal, the anger, is treated as the flaw the industry is here to correct.

The fur trade removes the layer and sells the coat. The beauty industry removes the layer and sells her back to herself, thinner, smoother, quieter, younger. Same procedure. Different receipt.

She is not being restored. She is being processed.

The skin coming off in this photograph is not the woman falling apart. It is the industry finally showing its work.

posts.caption:
They didn’t sell you a product. They sold you a word.

Clean. Natural. Conscious. Eco. Green. Five adjectives that built a decade of consumer trust and did not need to prove a single thing.

73% of people changed their habits based on those words. 14% checked whether the words were true. 60% of the claims turned out to be unsubstantiated.

The lie was not accidental. It was the marketing budget.

Statutory definitions are now coming. False claims will carry penalties. Transparency is becoming non-negotiable.

The next decade will not run on adjectives.

FERAL FEMME · Dismantling the Propaganda.

Sources: Pew · Reuters Institute · Digital Services Act · EU Green Claims Directive

posts.caption:
Remember where you come from.

That is what the sign said. It is also what the industry has spent centuries trying to make you forget.

Where you come from is the woman who marched before you and was arrested. And her mother, who marched and was ignored. And the one before her, who did not march because she was not allowed to leave the house. Where you come from is the animal your grandmother was told to be quiet like, obedient, useful, replaceable. Where you come from is the body that built the world without being paid for it, and was then handed the bill.

You are not the beginning of anything. You are the debt collector.

The march ends. The street empties. The cans get swept up. The graffiti gets painted over. The industry counts on that. Not on defeating you, on outlasting you. On your exhaustion becoming your amnesia. On your daughter having to learn everything from scratch, because no one wrote it down.

We are the ones who stay behind and write it down.

Every march. Every name. Every body the receipt was never printed for.

The paper trail is the movement.

FERAL FEMME · Dismantling the Propaganda.

The pattern has not changed. The subject has not been asked. The industry has just changed the tag colour.

She is not the costume. She is the file.

The ban was a press release. The testing kept going.

The EU banned animal testing on cosmetics in 2013. The brands printed cruelty-free on the box. The chemical-safety law kept testing the exact same ingredients, under a different file name.

A peer-reviewed study identified 3,206 REACH dossiers for chemicals used in cosmetics. 63 of them logged animal tests after the ban.

The product is cruelty-free.
The ingredient is not.
The label is the loophole.

SWIPE for the case file →

You were not lied to. You were filed under the wrong regulation.

the market takes over.

FERAL FEMME exists to expose the system behind the standards,
the marketing, the conditioning, and the industries built on it.

Because the wild was never the problem.
The cage was.

posts.caption:

Animals are still trapped, bred, confined and killed for fashion, beauty, and novelty industries worldwide.

When suffering is repackaged as aesthetic, it becomes easier to sell.

Captivity isn’t luxury.

then sold you the solution.

posts.caption:
Rabbits are used in cosmetic testing for control, not accuracy.
They’re chosen because their biology makes resistance unlikely and their pain easier to manage within the testing process.

If distress interferes with results, it’s considered a problem, not the suffering itself.
That’s how convenience becomes the priority.

In systems like this, efficiency is rewarded.
Suffering is simply absorbed into the process.

The discomfort you feel reading this is intentional.
Education removes consent from cruelty.
